unit.title: Finite Discrete-Time Signals and Reliable Convolution Software
unit.audience: A strong algorithms student beginning deliberate software-engineering practice
prerequisites: Comfort with Python functions, classes, and unittest
No prior signals-and-systems course material is assumed for the software task
unit.purpose: Build and test a small finite-signal API, implement direct and sparsity-aware linear convolution, and produce reproducible correctness and performance evidence.

included: Linear convolution by two independently structured implementations
API contracts, input validation, deterministic unit and property-style tests
A fixed-seed microbenchmark and a short engineering report
excluded: Differential equations, frequency response, sampling theory, and feedback control
Any claim to reproduce an official EE120 lecture, assignment, or lab

learning_objectives: Translate mathematical indexing conventions into an explicit Python API contract
Implement direct and sparsity-aware convolution with consistent edge-case behavior
Use an independent implementation, invariants, and deterministic generated cases as correctness evidence
Separate asymptotic reasoning from measured performance and report limitations honestly
Package code, tests, evidence, and provenance so another engineer can reproduce the work

required: All expected learner outputs are present
The submitted benchmark is reproducible and explicitly labeled as learner-produced evidence
The report and comprehension responses are independently assessed against examiner_only/RUBRIC.md

whole_course_completion.requires: A separately expanded, provenance-backed unit graph plus successful validation of every later required unit; those units are not yet defined or available.

completion_policy.failed_or_partial_work: Retain the attempt and its evidence with a failed or incomplete label; do not promote it to unit or course completion.

provenance.derivation_note: The catalog title, description, prerequisites, language, and resource locators informed the kickoff. The unit design and learner materials are newly authored and are not represented as UC Berkeley content.
